Framework for modeling transitions from improvement within fixed possibility spaces to modifying mechanisms that determine reachable possibilities; introduces adaptive depth, reachable future transformation spaces, generator modification capacity and evolutionary velocity as a proposed approach.

Open research framework; contributions span formalization, theory, empirical validation, historical cases, measurement, simulations, documentation and critical review; goal is increasingly precise testable claims.

Prefer trajectory variables over new ontological categories; ask whether a proposed entity is a genuinely new causal mechanism with measurable predictions or a derivative/transformation of existing variables.
Do not use capability growth alone as evidence of evolutionary acceleration.
Proposed changes should identify whether they modify ontology, dynamics, measurement or empirical evidence, and state what becomes newly measurable, predictable or explainable.

Simulation/computational code contributions should include assumptions, reproducible parameters, metric explanations, limitations and expected behavior; code should support theory, not replace explanation.
What determines the evolution of the function that generates evolution?
Adaptive Evolutionary Dynamics
Framework for studying transitions from improvement inside a fixed possibility space to modification of mechanisms determining reachable possibilities.
Major capability transitions are preceded by changes in the processes that generate future capability.
Capability growth is not evolutionary acceleration; a system can become more capable without becoming better at becoming more capable.
Delta G_m -> Delta Omega -> Delta C: generator mechanism changes, future-improvement rate changes, observable capability accelerates afterward.
E_t -> O_t -> M_t -> pi_t -> u_t -> E_(t+1), with O_t=H(E_t), M_(t+1)=U(M_t,O_t), u_t=pi_t(M_t,V_t), E_(t+1)=F(E_t,u_t), X_(t+1)=F_X(X_t,E_t,u_t).

Omega is not capability, complexity, intelligence, growth rate or resource quantity; it denotes internally generated acceleration of capability-generation capacity.
